section: Social Studies · Ch52 — Methodology of Teaching Social Studies
subject: Social Studies
stem: For teaching history to young primary-level pupils, narrating events as an engaging story with characters and sequence is preferred mainly because it:

options.option_text: Matches the child's interest and helps retention through a memorable narrative structure
Removes the need for any historical accuracy
Is only useful for teaching mathematics
Replaces the need for any further discussion or questions

explanation: The storytelling method exploits children's natural interest in narratives, aiding memory and engagement — while still requiring factual accuracy and follow-up discussion, not replacing them.

stem: Taking pupils to visit a local historical monument or a Gram Panchayat office as part of a Social Studies lesson is an example of the:
explanation: Field trips give pupils direct, first-hand experience of real institutions/sites, making abstract civic or historical concepts concrete — a hallmark of activity-based Social Studies pedagogy.

section: Social Studies · Ch52 — Methodology of Teaching Social Studies
subject: Social Studies
stem: The most effective way to develop map-reading skills in pupils is to:

options.option_text: Have pupils actively locate places, trace routes, and even draw simple maps themselves
Have pupils only listen to the teacher describe map features verbally
Show a map once at the start of the year and never refer to it again
Avoid maps entirely and rely only on textbook text

explanation: Active, repeated practice — locating, tracing, and drawing — builds durable map skills, consistent with learning-by-doing; passive verbal description alone is much less effective for spatial skills.

section: Social Studies · Ch52 — Methodology of Teaching Social Studies
subject: Social Studies
stem: When teaching a topic like 'causes of the freedom struggle', encouraging pupils to debate different viewpoints and reach a reasoned conclusion primarily fosters:

options.option_text: Critical thinking and the ability to evaluate multiple perspectives
Rote memorisation of a single fixed viewpoint

explanation: The discussion method actively engages pupils in weighing evidence and viewpoints, developing critical thinking — precisely the higher-order skill rote memorisation of a single narrative would bypass.
